issues.legal_issue: A final judgment may be set aside in a separate suit alleging fraud only when the fraud is pleaded with necessary particulars and proved by cogent evidence.
material_facts: A civil court had apportioned compensation between the claimants and the village body, and that judgment was not appealed.
A later suit sought to set aside that judgment on the ground that the claimants’ lease had been created through collusion with the village body’s former head.
The suit alleged no particulars explaining how the fraud had been committed.

The lease proposal and its acceptance were approved by the competent authority, the land was granted after an open auction, and the claimants took possession and cultivated it; revenue records supported their possession.
The evidence did not establish the alleged collusion or fraud.
issues.conclusion: The alleged fraud was neither pleaded with the necessary particulars nor proved, so the final judgment could not be set aside on that ground and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Fraud must be pleaded with necessary particulars and proved by cogent evidence; a court cannot infer fraud contrary to the record. The earlier compensation apportionment under Sections 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 had become final, and the later suit concerned only whether that judgment was procured by fraud. The Court applied the settled pleading-and-proof principle, consistent with Ranganayakamma v. K.S. Prakash, and held that the authorities cited for the proposition that a decree obtained by fraud is a nullity did not assist without proof of fraud.

rule.if: separate_suit_challenges_final_judgment_for_fraud and fraud_particulars_absent and (official_approvals_and_open_auction_occurred and possession_records_supported_claim) and alleged_fraud_not_proved

predicates.separate_suit_challenges_final_judgment_: A claimant brought a separate suit seeking to set aside a judgment that had become final, alleging that it was procured by fraud.
predicates.fraud_particulars_absent: The claimant alleging fraud did not plead particulars explaining how the fraud was committed.
predicates.official_approvals_and_open_auction_occu: The proposed grant and its acceptance received competent-authority approval, and the land was granted through an open auction.
predicates.possession_records_supported_claim: The alleged beneficiaries took possession and used the land, and official records supported their possession.
predicates.alleged_fraud_not_proved: The evidence did not establish the alleged fraud or collusion.

issues.definition: When a separate suit challenges a final judgment for fraud, the judgment remains undisturbed if the allegation lacks particulars and the evidence, including the approval and possession records, does not prove fraud.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of an executed and registered lease deed does not by itself prevent a person who acted on an agreement of lease and took possession from relying on the protection of that possession.
material_facts: The village body approved a proposal to lease the land, and the competent authority approved the proposed grant and the successful auction bid.
The claimants were put in possession after the bid was accepted and continued in possession while cultivating the land.
No lease deed was executed and registered.
issues.conclusion: The claimants could rely on Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 to protect their possession despite the absence of an executed and registered lease deed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 can protect a person in possession who has acted on a contract even though the contemplated instrument was not executed and registered. The Court relied on Maneklal Mansukhbhai v. Hormusji Jamshedji Ginwalla & Sons for an agreement of lease and Hamzabi v. Syed Karimuddin for the protection of possession under a contract. It held that Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R.N. Kapoor and C.M. Beena v. P.N. Ramachandra Rao did not assist the challenge on these facts.

rule.if: dispute_involves_unregistered_lease and competent_authority_approved_lease_grant and land_granted_after_auction and claimant_took_possession_under_agreement

predicates.dispute_involves_unregistered_lease: A dispute concerns rights asserted under an agreement to lease for which no lease deed was executed and registered.
predicates.competent_authority_approved_lease_grant: The proposed lease grant received approval from the authority competent to approve it.
predicates.land_granted_after_auction: The land was granted to the successful bidder after an auction.
predicates.claimant_took_possession_under_agreement: The claimant took possession of the land pursuant to the agreed grant.

issues.definition: When an unregistered lease agreement was approved, followed by an auction grant and possession under the agreement, the claimant’s possession is protected.
